title: Cylindrical object
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety, zero, and negative ninety degrees, and the translation vector to zero, zero, and zero. On the first face, draw the first loop which consists of a single circle centered at the coordinates zero point zero one eight two, zero point zero one eight two, with a radius of zero point zero one eight two. Apply a scale factor of zero point zero three six five to the entire sketch. Rotate the scaled sketch using the same Euler angles and translate it using the same translation vector. Extrude the sketch along the normal direction by zero point seven five units, ensuring that no extrusion occurs in the opposite direction and that the operation results in a new solid body. The final dimensions of the cylindrical object will be a length of zero point zero three six four five eight three three three three three three three six, a width of zero point zero three six four five eight three three three three three three three six, and a height of zero point seven five. This process ensures the creation of a cylindrical object with a flat top and bottom, a smooth surface, and a uniform diameter throughout its length.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Set the center and radius of the circle
center = (0.0182, 0.0182)
radius = 0.0182

# Create a circle in the XY plane
r = r.center(center[0], center[1]).circle(radius)

# Extrude the circle to create a cylinder
extrude_depth = 0.75
r = r.extrude(extrude_depth)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the cylinder 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
